title: Einstein's Gravity Just Passed a Quantum Test
mediaSource: quantum atom free fall gravity experiment atom chip Einstein equivalence principle

scenes.title: Does Einstein's gravity work in the quantum world?
scenes.narration: Einstein's gravity works extremely well for planets and stars. But does the same principle still hold for atoms that behave like quantum waves?

scenes.title: Scientists measured falling quantum atoms
scenes.narration: An international team measured how the quantum phase of freely falling atoms changed under gravity with high precision.

scenes.title: The result matched Einstein's prediction
scenes.narration: The observed shift matched what Einstein's equivalence principle predicts when it is applied to a quantum object.

scenes.title: Free fall can make gravity seem to disappear
scenes.narration: The equivalence principle says that an observer in free fall should locally feel weightless. This experiment found that the same idea remains consistent with quantum behavior.

scenes.title: This is not quantum gravity yet
scenes.narration: The result does not prove that gravity itself is quantum. But it directly tests the boundary where quantum mechanics and Einstein's theory meet.

scenes.title: A century-old idea survived a smaller world
scenes.narration: Einstein's equivalence principle passed this test even for tiny quantum objects. The next challenge is to repeat similar tests with much heavier systems.
